title: What does PaymentChannelCreate do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of PaymentChannelCreate and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, PaymentChannelCreate locks XRP in a channel for repeated payments to a specified destination. [1]

The sender supplies a public key for claim signatures and a SettleDelay for the closure process. Off-ledger claims can update authorization without a new ledger transaction for every increment. Creating a channel does not mean the destination has received its entire funded amount; redemption and final closure determine the actual transfers. [1]

The PaymentChannelCreate reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using PaymentChannelCreate, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
